standard: Acceptable visible refinement at application scale; not a numerical quality rating or production release approval.

front.note: The full front seat welt now forms a continuous seated loop without the previous missing span or loose corner tails; softened padding and connected metal supports improve the original plain chair.

rear.note: The rear run now follows the cushion rather than floating above its left corner. The two back uprights and capped leg ends remain clearly connected.

detail.note: Full-size detail shows a complete rounded piping cross-section at the seat edge. Small waviness in the white line remains a handcrafted limitation, acceptable at application scale.

underside.note: The dark seat pan and four metal legs remain coherent from below, with no new detached geometry or exposed cushion hole.

clay.note: The clay view preserves the recognizable squared chair silhouette, rounded seat and back corners, arm clearances, and floor contacts.

front.note: The pale ceramic finish and softened rims are modest refinements, but the strongly faceted tubes and six pointed planar flower petals still read as a coarse placeholder; further geometry work is required.

rear.note: The staggered original vase heights and independent stems remain intact. The rear silhouette still exposes flat star-shaped petals rather than constructed flowers.

detail.note: Full-size detail confirms each bloom consists of thin pointed planes around a blunt cylindrical center. Rounded cupped petal construction is needed within the original bounds.

underside.note: Full-size underside shows open outer bottom rings and the lower stems visible through the vessels. The source ring helper has an inner floor but no exterior bottom closure; add a closed ceramic base.

clay.note: The clay view retains three recognizable hollow vase mouths, but coarse circular walls and star-like flowers remain clearly visible; this candidate is not yet accepted as a catalog improvement.

front.note: The oval recessed bowl, narrow brass frame and stone shelf remain distinct, with softened material response improving the original dark flat preview while retaining its compact console construction.

rear.note: The rear faucet rail and brass uprights stay aligned behind the basin; no new detached bracket or obstructed bowl opening is visible.

detail.note: Full-size detail shows restrained stone variation over the curved bowl and lower shelf, rounded rim edges and coherent rail intersections. The sparse faucet is an inherited stylistic limitation.

underside.note: The lower shelf has a continuous underside and four connected posts, while the basin remains supported by its surrounding rails; no new opening or floating member is visible.

clay.note: The clay view confirms the original oval hollow basin and open rectangular frame silhouette remain clear, with consistent foot contact and shelf thickness.

front.note: The original cream diamond pattern remains legible and correctly placed; fine textile surface response and the visible bound edge give a modest improvement without replacing the authored artwork.

rear.note: The reverse camera angle preserves the same diamond layout, border and rectangular footprint without stretched or mirrored islands.

detail.note: Full-size detail retains the deliberately irregular dark motifs and fine edge fringe; the cream field reads softly woven without oversized normal bumps. Dense modeled pile is not claimed.

underside.note: The underside remains a flat continuous dark backing with a thin pale edge, without holes or unintended separate geometry.

clay.note: The clay view preserves a thin, flat rectangular rug and stable corners; the accepted improvement is restrained surface treatment rather than a new sculpted silhouette.

front.note: The original blue border, lotus flowers and muted green field remain intact; gentle textile variation gives a clearer fabric reading while preserving the authored composition.

rear.note: The alternate angle keeps all corner floral motifs and geometric border lines aligned, with no visible atlas shift or new footprint distortion.

detail.note: Full-size detail shows fine grain in the green field and crisp original lotus contours, with a thin fringe along the short edge. Relief remains intentionally subtle at room scale.

underside.note: The dark backing is continuous beneath the thin pale binding, and no underside fragment or unintended protrusion is visible.

clay.note: The clay view remains a clean thin rectangular slab with consistent edge thickness and no lifted corners; no volumetric pile improvement is implied.

front.note: The original orange, cream and dark-blue geometric motifs remain recognizable; restrained woven response and edge fringe improve the textile reading without changing the pattern.

rear.note: The second angle retains motif positions and border widths with a flat footprint; no mirrored or sliding texture island is visible.

detail.note: Full-size detail preserves the small colored weave lines inside the original zigzags and diamonds. The regular print remains an inherited artwork choice, with no coarse procedural bumps.

underside.note: The underside has a single continuous dark backing and narrow bound perimeter; there is no new geometry below the intended rug thickness.

clay.note: The clay view confirms a thin flat rug with stable rectangular edges and corners, suitable for the preserved floor placement envelope.

front.note: The centered medallion and original blue floral field remain intact; softer textile response and a readable bound edge provide a modest refinement of the existing detailed rug.

rear.note: The reverse view preserves the medallion orientation and nested border spacing, without an atlas seam or distorted outer rectangle.

detail.note: Full-size detail retains the intricate original floral artwork and fine edge fringe. The surface is softly matte; individual knotted pile is not modeled or claimed.

underside.note: The continuous dark backing stays inside the pale rectangular perimeter, with no new holes, detached fringe strip or underside protrusion.

clay.note: The clay view preserves the original flat thin construction, even corners and floor-facing surface; this approval covers restrained material refinement at application scale.
